title: tool-calling: improve execution ergonomics for parallel multi-tool calls and result injection
author: Leah Patel
commit_summary: Initial implementation of parallel tool execution executor and coordinator
Add result-injection pipeline and deterministic retry semantics
Stabilize streaming path to prevent interleaved chunks during parallel injections
OpenAI-compat: extend function-calling wrapper to expose parallel results and retry codes
description:
Context: Customers are increasingly using multi-tool and parallel tool call patterns (e.g. search + calculator + mailer) as part of a single assistant turn. Current behavior had two ergonomic gaps: (1) tool results could arrive in arbitrary order and be injected into the model in a way that caused confusing streaming interleaving, and (2) retry semantics for transient tool failures were ad-hoc and often required manual orchestration in the application layer.

Motivation: Improve developer ergonomics for tool-calling by providing a first-class parallel execution path that guarantees deterministic result-injection ordering, safe streaming integration (no interleaved token corruption), and opinionated retry policies surfaced through the OpenAI-compat function-calling layer. This reduces application-side plumbing and makes complex multi-tool flows more reliable out-of-the-box.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces a ParallelExecutor that runs multiple tool invocations concurrently while tracking logical dependencies and producing a stable injection order.
- Adds ResultInjection pipeline that serializes tool outputs into structured blocks the runtime can stream without interleaving partial tokens.
- Implements retry policies (exponential backoff with idempotency windows) for transient tool errors, with configurable overrides per-tool.
- Extends the OpenAI-compat function-calling wrapper to accept a list of function calls and return a consistent, ordered response payload (including per-call status, retries, and final outputs).
- Adds SDK surface: python client helper execute_tools_parallel(...) that mirrors the new compat behavior.

Checklist: 
- [x] ParallelExecutor MVP implemented + unit tests
- [x] ResultInjection streaming stability fixes
- [x] OpenAI compatibility layer extended for multi-call responses
- [x] SDK helper and API docs updates
- [x] Metrics emitted for tool latency, retry count, and injection lag
- [x] Safety review for tool output isolation (Priya)

Files changed (high level):
- server/tool_executor/parallel_executor.py: core coordinator, worker pool abstraction, deterministic ordering algorithm (stable sort by declared dependency then by call index).
- server/tool_executor/result_injection.py: creates framed injection blocks, escape rules, and buffering to prevent partial-token streaming across injections.
- server/handler/streaming.py: streaming glue updated to consume framed injection blocks and emit them atomically to streaming clients. Added tests to validate no interleaving with concurrent chat updates.
- openai_compat/function_calling.py: new API compat surface that accepts list[FunctionCall] and returns list[FunctionResult], preserving order and exposing retry metadata. Backwards compatible with single-call path.
- sdk/python/redwood/client.py: add execute_tools_parallel convenience method + docs string and tests.
- tests/test_tool_parallel.py: covers concurrency, retry behavior, and streaming stability.
- docs/tool-calling.md: documents new parallel flow, SDK examples, config knobs (max_concurrency, max_retries, idempotency_window).
- observability/tool_calls_metrics.yaml: adds metrics for parallel executor queue depth and retry counts.

Review conversation (summary):
- Ethan: asked for explicit guarantees around ordering and whether user-provided dependency graphs are honored. Response: ParallelExecutor uses declared dependency edges first, then stable index order; added unit tests and doc section clarifying semantics.
- Priya: requested safety audit for injection boundaries (ensure no accidental prompt contamination). Response: Added framed injection blocks + escaping and a regression test that simulates malicious tool outputs. Priya approved after tests.
- Rafael: pointed out a potential edge-case where all tools fail repeatedly and executor could spin. Response: added exponential backoff + idempotency window and a circuit-breaker that short-circuits after a configurable failure threshold. Rafael approved.

CI summary: initial CI run hit a flaky streaming test (race in streaming.py around chunk flush). I pushed a follow-up commit that serializes flushes in the result_injection pipeline. Re-ran; all checks passed (unit tests, linters, integration with openai_compat harness).

Backward compatibility and migration notes: The OpenAI-compat wrapper remains backward compatible for single function call flows. Multi-call behavior is opt-in via the new execute_tools_parallel helper or by passing a list to the compat endpoint. Defaults for retries and concurrency are conservative (max_concurrency=3, max_retries=2) to avoid surprising cost spikes.

Release notes: "Improved tool-calling ergonomics: stable parallel tool execution, deterministic result injection order, safer streaming with framed injections, and configurable retry policies. New Python SDK helper: execute_tools_parallel()."

Merge outcome: squash-merged to main. This lays the groundwork for a follow-up PR that will surface a TypeScript SDK helper and add an advanced server-side planner for dependency resolution.

Priya Nair: safety review - ensure no prompt injection via tool outputs -> addressed with framing and escaping, added regression tests.
Rafael Gomez: add circuit-breaker for repeated failures to avoid executor spin -> implemented and tested.
